How to use Molecule to Biosphere

  • Journey through life: the Journey button at the top walks through the history of life in order, from the first cells to today. Every big idea in the course appears at the moment in life’s history when it first mattered. Use Next and Back (or the ← → keys).
  • Zoom through the levels of life: scroll, pinch, or drag the gold knob on the ruler at the left to go from a DNA molecule, through proteins, organelles, a cell, a leaf and a whole tree, to an Adirondack ecosystem, New York State and the whole biosphere.
  • Drag the scene to rotate it. Tap labels to learn more and open activities.
  • The Here tab lists the standards that fit the level you’re looking at. The Standards tab holds all 30 assessed on the Regents, each with an activity, the full standard and its core ideas.
  • Choose Regents or Honors with ⚙. Content marked Honors goes beyond what the Regents exam assesses. In Regents mode it is tucked behind a dashed “Honors extension” button you can still open.
  • Easier reading: the Aa Easier reading button at the top (or ⚙ Settings) rewrites the Journey and every standard in shorter, simpler sentences, with key words, a Regents tip, tap-to-define help for underlined words, and 🔊 read-aloud.
  • Practice: Regents-style clusters for every standard, and a map of every cluster from the released Life Science: Biology Regents exams, linked to the official PDFs.
  • Labs: full-screen interactive labs for every unit, including versions of the three required investigations (Balancing Act, Lactose Tolerance and For the Birds).
  • Placemarks: on the globe and the New York map, tap a placemark (the Galápagos, Yellowstone’s wolves, Onondaga Lake and more) for its story and practice questions.
  • My results: the ✓ button on the Journey card makes a summary you can hand in.
  • Keyboard: + and − zoom, arrow keys rotate, Home returns to Earth.
